translations.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the chosen exiles scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, through sanctification by the Spirit, for obedience and the shedding of the blood of Jesus Christ: may grace and peace be multiplied among you.
Blessed is the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, according to his great mercy, has given us new birth into a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,
into an inheritance that is imperishable, undefiled, and unfading, kept in heaven for you,
who were guarded by the power of God through faith for the salvation prepared to be revealed in the last times.
In this you will rejoice, though now, for a little while, as circumstances require, you have been grieved by various trials.
For the proof of your faith is more precious than perishable gold tested by fire, and is found to bring praise, glory, and honor at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
You love him whom you have not seen. Though you do not see him now, you believe in him and rejoice with an indescribable and glorious joy,
receiving the fulfillment of your faith, the salvation of your souls.
The prophets sought and investigated this salvation, prophesying about the grace that was to come to you.
They investigated what time and what kind of time the Spirit of Christ within them was foretelling, when he testified beforehand to Christ’s sufferings and the glories that would follow.

It was revealed to them that they were serving not themselves but us in these things, which have now been reported to you by those who proclaimed the good news to you through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven—things that angels desired to see, even dimly.
Therefore, brace your minds, remain alert, and place your hope fully in the grace that will come to you at the revelation of Jesus Christ.
As obedient children, do not conform yourselves to the desires you formerly had in your ignorance,
but, just as the one who called you is holy, you too must be holy in all your conduct.
For it is written, “Be holy, because I am holy.”
And if you call him Father who judges impartially according to each person's deeds, then spend the time of your stay here as foreigners in fear.
Know that you were redeemed from the futile way of life inherited from your ancestors, not with perishable things made of silver or gold,
but with the precious blood of Christ, like that of a lamb without blemish or stain.
He was foreknown before the beginning of the world and was revealed at the end of the times for your sake,
you who through him believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.
Purify your souls through obedience to the truth for sincere brotherly love, and love one another earnestly from a pure heart.
You have been born anew, not from perishable seed but from imperishable seed, through the living and everlasting word of God.
For all flesh is like grass, and all human glory is like the flower of grass. The grass withered, and the flower fell.
And the word of the Lord remains forever. This is the word that was proclaimed to you as good news.
Therefore, put away all wickedness, all deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and all slander,
Like newborn infants, long for the pure, spiritual milk, so that through it you may grow toward salvation.
if you have tasted that the Lord is good.
Come to him, the living rock, who, though rejected by human beings, is chosen and precious in God’s sight.
And you, like living stones, are being built into a spiritual temple, to be an undefiled priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For it is indeed written in Scripture: “Look, I am laying in Zion a chosen stone, a precious cornerstone, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.”
For you, then, who believe, he is a precious stone; but for unbelievers, “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,”
and “a stone that makes people fall and a rock of stumbling.” They stumble because they disobey the word, which is also what they were appointed to do.
But you are a chosen race, a kingdom, a priesthood, a holy nation, a people belonging to God, so that you may offer your virtues to him who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light.
Once you were not a people, but now you are God's people; once you had not received mercy, but now you have found mercy.
Beloved, I urge you, as strangers and exiles, to turn away from bodily desires, which wage war against your souls,
and to show honorable conduct among the Gentiles, so that, although they slander you as evildoers, they may observe your good deeds and glorify God on the day of visitation.
Submit to every human institution for the Lord's sake, whether to the king as one who holds supreme authority,
or to governors as those sent by him to punish evildoers and praise those who do good.
For it is God's will that those who do good should silence the ignorance of foolish people.
Live as free people, but do not use your freedom as a pretext for evil; instead, live as servants of God.
Honor everyone, love the brotherhood, fear God, and honor kings.
Servants, submit to your masters in everything with reverence, not only to those who are kind and gentle, but also to those who are unreasonable.
For it is pleasing to God if someone with a good conscience endures suffering unjustly.
For what credit is there if you sin, are punished, and endure it? But if you do good, suffer, and endure it, that is pleasing to God.
For you were called to this very thing, because Christ also died for you and left you an example, so that you might follow in his footsteps.
He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth.
When he was slandered, he did not slander in return; when he suffered, he made no threats, but entrusted himself to the Judge who judges justly.
He carried our sins in his own body onto the wood of the cross, so that we might be freed from sins and live in righteousness. By his wounds you were healed.
For you were like sheep that had gone astray, but now you have returned to the Shepherd and Overseer of your souls.
Likewise, wives, submit to your own husbands, so that, if they disobey the word, they may be won over even without a word through their wives' conduct,
when they observe your pure and reverent conduct.
Let your adornment not be outward, with braids and gold-woven hair ornaments or ornate clothing,
but let it be the hidden person of the heart, with the imperishable quality of a submissive and quiet spirit, which is highly precious before God.
For this is how the women who hoped in God once adorned themselves, submitting to their own husbands.
Just as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him her lord, you became her children, doing good and neither being anxious nor fearing any terror.
Likewise, husbands should live with their wives with understanding, giving women honor as the weaker vessel and as fellow heirs of the grace of life, so that your prayers may not be hindered.
Above all, be of one mind, sympathetic, loving toward your brothers and sisters, compassionate, and humble.
Do not repay evil for evil or slander for slander, but instead give a blessing, for you were called to this very thing, so that you might inherit a blessing.
For whoever wishes to love life and see good days must keep his tongue from evil and his lips from speaking deceit.
Let him turn away from evil and do good; let him seek peace and pursue it.
For the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, and his ears attend to their prayers, but the face of the Lord is against evildoers.
And who will harm you if you are zealous for what is good?
But even if you suffer for righteousness, you are blessed. Do not fear their threats or be troubled.
But regard the Lord himself, Christ, as holy in your hearts. Be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks for an explanation of your hope, but with gentleness and reverence.
Maintain a gentle disposition, so that when they speak evil of you, those who slander your good conduct in Christ may be put to shame.
For it is better for those who do good to suffer, if they wish to do so in accordance with God's will, than for those who do evil.
For Christ also died once for sins on our behalf, the righteous one for the unrighteous, to bring us near to God. Although he died in the flesh, he is alive in the spirit.
In that spirit he also went and preached to the spirits who were in prison.
They had once rebelled, when God's patience bore with them in the days of Noah, while the ark was being built. In it a few—that is, about eight souls—were saved from the water.
Corresponding to this, baptism will also save you—not the removal of dirt from the body, but the presentation of a good conscience before God through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.
He is at God's right hand, having gone into heaven, with angels, authorities, and powers subject to him.
Since Christ suffered in the flesh for us, arm yourselves also with the same resolve, for whoever suffers in the flesh ceases from sin.
So that he may live the rest of his time no longer according to human desires, but according to God's will.
For the time that has passed is enough for doing the will of the Gentiles, who walked in lustfulness, desires, drunkenness, debauchery, drinking bouts, and unlawful idol worship.
Because of this they are estranged, do not join you in the same excess of disorderly living, and speak abusively.
They will give an account to the one who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
For this very purpose a promise has also been made to the dead, so that they may be judged in the flesh according to human standards, but live in the spirit according to God.
The end of all things has drawn near. Therefore be sensible and stay alert in prayer.
Above all, have earnest love for one another, because love covers a multitude of sins.
Be hospitable to one another without grumbling.
As each person has received a gift, use it to serve one another, as good stewards of God's varied grace.

If anyone speaks, let it be as God's utterances. If anyone serves, let it be with the strength that God supplies, so that God may be glorified in everything through Jesus Christ, to whom belong glory and power forever and ever. Amen.
Beloved, do not regard the fiery ordeal that comes upon you to test you as something strange, as though something unfamiliar were happening to you.
Instead, rejoice as those who share in Christ's sufferings, so that when his glory is revealed you may also rejoice with exultation.
But even if you are insulted because of the name of Christ, you are blessed, because the name of glory and power, and the Spirit of God, rest upon you.
Let none of you suffer as a murderer, a thief, a wrongdoer, or someone who meddles in other people's affairs.
But if someone suffers as a Christian, let that person not be ashamed, but glorify God by this name.
For it is time for judgment to begin with the house of God. And if it begins with us first, what will be the end of those who did not obey the gospel of God?
And if the righteous person is barely saved, where will the ungodly person and the sinner be found?
Therefore, let those who suffer according to God's will entrust their souls to the faithful Creator by doing good.
Now I appeal to the elders as a fellow elder and a witness of Christ's sufferings, who also shares in the glory that is to be revealed:
Shepherd the flock of God that is among you, watching over it not reluctantly but willingly, according to God; not for greedy gain, but eagerly.
Do not lord it over those entrusted to you, but be examples to the flock,
so that when the Chief Shepherd appears, you may receive the unfading crown of glory.
Likewise, you younger people, submit to the elders. All of you, be humble toward one another, for God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.
Humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that he may exalt you in due time.
Cast all your cares upon him, because he cares for you.
Be alert and keep watch, because your adversary Satan roars like a lion, prowling around and seeking someone to devour.
Resist him, firm in faith, knowing that the same experiences of suffering are being endured by your fellow believers throughout the world.

And the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, after you have shared in suffering for a little while, will himself restore you, strengthen you, and establish you firmly.
To him be dominion and glory forever. Amen.
Through Silvanus, whom I regard as a faithful brother, I have written briefly to you, to encourage you and to testify that this is indeed the true grace of God, in which you are to stand firm.
The church in Babylon, chosen together with you, greets you, and so does Mark, my son.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. Peace to all of you who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.
